page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture. The instance provides 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs with a one-to-one thread-to-core mapping, utilizing the Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture clocked at 2.8 GHz. The cache configuration features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. System memory is sized at 768 GB, offering an 8:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of 5,700 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, accompanied by a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory throughput. Multi-core execution is in the top tier, shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 163,551.91, a Geekbench multi-core score of 25,998.0, and a Clang software compilation score of 92,597.0. Memory subsystems deliver high transfer rates, measuring 481.08 GB/sec in uncached large-block reads and 217.77 GB/sec in writes. Database and key-value benchmarks also show top-tier output, reaching 197.57 million Redis SET operations per second and high PassMark database operations scores. In contrast, single-threaded processing reflects median performance, with single-core stress-ng (1,706.48) and Geekbench (1,888.0) falling within average bands.

By omitting discrete GPUs and maximizing CPU core count alongside large physical memory and high-capacity NVMe drives, the instance delivers balanced resource density. The integrated NVMe storage eliminates external volume latency for scratch datasets, while the 40 Gbps network baseline supports high node-to-node communication. The r8gd.24xlarge is suitable for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large relational databases, distributed Redis or Memcached clusters, heavy ETL pipelines, and parallelized data processing systems.
